zotero.abstractNote: Cognitive-behavioral therapy (CBT) is the first-line psychological treatment for obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD). However, treatment response is heterogeneous, and predictors of outcome are poorly understood. We investigated whether clinical and neuroimaging data can predict CBT outcome in OCD. We analyzed data from 108 patients with OCD who underwent CBT. Clinical predictors included baseline symptom severity, age, and duration of illness. Neuroimaging predictors included structural MRI (gray matter volume) and resting-state functional connectivity (rs-FC). We used machine learning models to predict treatment response (remission vs. non-remission). Our results indicate that clinical variables, but not neuroimaging data, significantly predicted CBT outcome. These findings suggest that clinical characteristics are more robust predictors of CBT response in OCD than current neuroimaging markers.
